note: Triennial election of the Castlederg rural district councillors, 1933. Thirteen divisions had one nomination each and were returned unopposed; 'There will be no election in the Castlederg district' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1933, p. 4). No nominations were received for Ardarver, Ballymongan and Clunahill and 'the retiring members will be deemed to be re-elected'; as no 1933 source names them, those three divisions are not recorded. No party labels are printed. No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 31 May 1933. At the new council's first meeting the Clerk announced a vacancy for Ardarver, its former member Mr. Alexander M'Sorley having been nominated for Corgary; the Council declared the vacancy and filled it by co-opting Mr. Wm. Young (Ulster Herald, 10 June 1933, p. 7), a co-option, not an election. Ballymongan and Clunahill are not recorded: the 1930 member for Ballymongan, Mr. Bernard Devine, was one of the names proposed for the Ardarver vacancy, so he was not then sitting, and no report read names either division's continuing member. Returned unopposed.
